body.note: New owned chapter (heading \chapter, toc P15 159 159.8) on conditional independence of sigma-algebras; the P16 duties remain in the editable P16 hosts.

changes.summary: Transformed-tuple clause of thm:p16-measurable-ci-calculus stated precisely (g(X,Z) independent of h(Y,Z) given Z; image of the conditional product law at z outside one null set).

Paragraph 'Measurable transformations': kernel pi of (X,Y) given Z, image kernel rho via thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure, product form outside the single null set N, return to the product-test definition by Fubini.
Paragraph 'The whole kernel model': topological induction proving independence of U_v from predecessors, K_v as their regular conditional law, and joint law P_K.
New lemma thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-root-exposure; random-parameter consequence of thm:p16-measurable-response-component stated with kappa, lambda, theta displays.

annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-root-exposure proof; response-component proof now cites root exposure and the moral bridge at the separation step, proves R d-separated from B in the exposed graph and the kernel-model form, and gives the full random-parameter derivation (L(R|B,C)=L(R|C) as kernels; substitution through thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure; signed case).

Opening of the fields proof cites the root-exposure lemma; cross-world field rewritten with Facts 1-6: Fact 1 puts every strict exposure descendant that is a mediator ancestor in D_M; Fact 5 proves the auxiliary mediator tuple is M_b; Fact 6 proves every vertex needed for Y outside C lies in D_Y with inputs exactly a,m.

changes.lines: 89-122, 156-159 (line numbers from the first run; shifted by this run, see the label anchors)
changes.summary: Source's reading of disturbances vs regression residuals (p. 104), Wright (1921) directionality and missing-arrow claims (pp. 103-104), autonomy as the meaning of 'structural' (Simon 1953; Koopmans 1953; p. 107), tied to the invariance stipulation.

changes.lines: 182-236 (line numbers from the first run; shifted by this run, see the label anchors)
changes.summary: Experimental risk ratio with nonzero-denominator boundary, intervention variance and other functionals, controlled distribution as marginal of the post-intervention law, source eqs. (8)-(9) and 'causal effect', controlled/experimental reading (p. 108), p. 107 justificatory and historical claims.

changes.lines: 424-433 (line numbers from the first run; shifted by this run, see the label anchors)
changes.summary: n. 8 attributions for Theorem 1 (Pearl 2000a p. 30; Pearl and Verma 1991; Kiiveri et al. 1984; Lauritzen 2001).

changes.lines: 334-457 (line numbers from the first run; shifted by this run, see the label anchors)
changes.summary: n. 8 Manipulation Theorem and Robins 1987 attributions; thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-five-variable (Fig. 3: eqs. (18)-(22) in finite form with positive-mass conditions for observational replacement) and the source's claims (direct estimability, adjustment by inspection, time-varying treatments: Robins 1986, Arjas and Parner 2004).
annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-five-variable.

changes.lines: 480-507 (line numbers from the first run; shifted by this run, see the label anchors)
changes.summary: Definition 2 attribution (Pearl 2000a, p. 77), gloss with the exact finite equivalence 'identified iff Q is a function of the observed law on the class' (proved inline), and the linear-parametric vs procedural contrast.

changes.lines: 547-592 (line numbers from the first run; shifted by this run, see the label anchors)
changes.summary: P(Z=z|do(X=x))=P(Z=z) display and pre-intervention-factor remark (p. 111); the two-assumption variant (p. 109) as thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-weak.
annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-weak.

thm:p16-measurable-interventions states K_v (delta_{t_v} at intervened vertices) as regular conditional law given all predecessors, defines K_v from lambda_v, and states the history-based law as the kernel model on the augmented graph with the global Markov property.

annex:p16.measurable-interventions: claim for any acyclic system with independent disturbances (kernel measurability, independence of the current disturbance from the predecessors, regular conditional law, induction with thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure and rectangle uniqueness); constant interventions (delta_{t_v}); history-based kernels with fresh uniform noise on a product space, kernel model on G^Q, thm:p16-measurable-global-markov applied.

Wright's disease/symptom illustration (eqs (1)-(2), n. 6, Fig. 1(a),(b), dashed double arrow), structural reading of diagram vs equations and the external/internal clause, disturbances as source of observed variation assessed qualitatively, missing-link encoding and 'causal, not associational' with experimental uncovering (tied to item 1 of thm:p16-causal-nonidentification), p. 107 central idea, autonomy.

Sec. 3.2 opening claims (SEM main vehicle; until recently; new ways of defining and estimating effects in nonlinear and nonparametric models; invariance for causal effects and counterfactuals); eq. (14) with its four claims; new thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-linear-effect.
annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-linear-effect (items 1-4 and the standardized forms (14), (3), (4)).
p. 113: (22) coincides with Robins (1987) G-computation; adjustment for treatment-affected covariates (Z3 affected by Z2), read off item 3.
p. 108 framing quotation and its relation to the exact-law criterion and to estimation.

p. 110 Markovian claim, non-Markovian conditions (sec. 3.3), end of sec. 3.2.2 graph claim; full observation and positivity as the finite qualification, linked to items 1 and 2 of thm:p16-causal-nonidentification.

p. 107 illustration (pointwise under do(Z=z,X=x)); p. 111 conclusions related to the example's hypotheses; normative orthogonality sentence quoted; two assumptions attributed to (13) only, the P(y|do(x)) variant marked as the handbook's own.
def:p16-causal-dag defines child, descendants and ancestor.

Source's kinship and path vocabulary (pp. 104-105) with the Fig. 1(b) two-path example; def:p15-w02c-p15-009-causal-diagram (disturbance vertices, solid/dashed arrows, dashed double arrows, kinship over all arrows, paths over edges of any kind); distinct-vertex precision marked as the handbook's; thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-diagram-paths.
annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-diagram-paths: kinship of disturbance vertices, acyclicity, agreement with G, exact enumeration of the paths of Fig. 1(a) and 1(b).

Path-analysis paragraph of p. 105: (i) Wright's graphical covariance rules as the source's historical claim, (3)-(4) as instances; (ii) algebra obscures origins for large models, with the path-by-path reading of (4) (handbook's observation); (iii) solving for path coefficients from observed covariances with the quoted proviso. thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-path-solve (beta = Cov/Var under the two assumptions; three observationally equal models with contrasts 2, 0, 0).
annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-path-solve.

p. 106 claims on the chain (seven assumptions, none testable alone, totality implies Z unassociated with Y in every stratum of X); seven-link enumeration marked as the handbook's reading; thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-testable (CI from the factorization, violating law, each single assumption compatible with every law, pairwise independence insufficient); link to d-separation and thm:p16-finite-global-markov.
annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-testable.

Pearl's Definition 1 related to def:p16-active-path; p. 106 illustration with disturbance vertices (printed U_X _||_ Y | Z identified as a misprint for U_Z _||_ Y | Z; U_Z _||_ Y | X); collider path U_Z->Z->X<-U_X; Berkson (1946) and the two coins; the 'main opening'/'almost all tests' claim; note 7 on dormant independence. New thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-diagram (five items).

annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-diagram: diagram factorization and global Markov via thm:p16-finite-global-markov; d-separations by path enumeration; the counterexample, Berkson computation and its variant; necessity and sufficiency of the chain's CI test (function-valued disturbances).
p. 110 'endless confusions in the literature' and note 15 (p. 124: beta as incremental causal effect, the attributions); finite difference form via item 1 of thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-linear-effect.

p. 112 stated purpose of the truncated factorization (derive causal quantities without equations or equation modification as in (11)-(13); write (18) instead of the five equations), related to thm:p16-causal-factorization and thm:p16-causal-truncation.

Adapted kernels, recursive combination, Proposition 2.46 and Definition 2.47 (Bayesian network (D,P), p. 66) in the source's notation; the departure (kernels kept in the model) stated, with two kernel models generating the same Bayesian network but different intervened laws.
Reason for the operationally defined upper quantile from the proof of Theorem 1.28 (pp. 19-20): non-unique quantiles, separate choices may destroy joint measurability.

p. 65 contrast with the undirected case; undirected (P),(L),(G), Proposition 2.37, Theorem 2.38 (Pearl and Paz) and (S5) reported with locators; new def:p15-w02c-p15-009-undirected-markov and thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-undirected-gap; p. 68 density strengthening ((F), Proposition 2.51, Lemma 2.52, Theorem 2.53) reported and related to the finite factorization.

annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-undirected-gap: (G)=>(L)=>(P) proved; three equal fair bits on the edgeless graph satisfy (P) but not (L), (G) or intersection; directed equivalence from the semigraphoid theorem.

Run b2: the 13 runs of 12 or more words shared with Pearl2009CausalOverview paraphrased; quotations reduced to at most 6 words (identification question, Markovian claim, graph-structure clause, orthogonality remark, external/internal clause, proviso). Copy guard now finds no run of 12 or more words in any of the four hosts.

New chapter sec:p15-w02c-p15-009-sigma-ci: def:p15-w02c-p15-009-sigma-ci; thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-sigma-ci-criteria (Lauritzen Lemma 2.6, Thm 2.9, Thm 2.10, Cors 2.11-2.12, Examples 2.2, 2.7, 2.13; item 7 agreement with def:p16-measurable-ci); thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-sigma-ci-rules (Thm 2.18 (A1)-(A4), Cor 2.20 (C1)-(C4)); thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-ci-tables (Example 2.3 tables, Example 2.19 intersection failure).

Full annex proofs for the three new theorems (Facts F1-F2; Dynkin argument; simple/nonnegative/signed extension; both directions of the one-sided criterion; weak union via the tower measurable-version rule; contraction; join identity sigma((Y,Z)); table computations; coin example).
One paragraph after def:p16-measurable-ci linking the sigma-algebra chapter.

proposed_decisions: Symbol overlap: check.py reports \mathcal{Z} (here \mathcal Z^+ in thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-five-variable) as out of registered scope; the intake row scopes it to that theorem.
Symbol overlap: \lambda denotes Lebesgue measure in annex:p16.measurable-kernel-randomization and a conditional law of B given C in thm:p16-measurable-response-component; both are locally declared.
The pre-existing out-of-scope notation findings for \mathbb P, \mathbb E, \mathcal U, \mathcal C in finite-causal-models.tex and \mathcal A in measurable-causal-graphs.tex predate this packet.

Symbol overlap:  eta is Pearl's path coefficient in sec:p16-causal-model-data and thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-linear-effect, while annex:p16.causal-nonidentification uses beta(d) as a weight function; both local.
Symbol overlap: \mathcal W_v (space of a generic disturbance) in annex:p16.measurable-interventions is reported by check.py as out of registered scope; intake row scopes it there.
Symbol overlap: kappa_X, kappa_Y in annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-testable are local target kernels, distinct from kappa of thm:p16-measurable-response-component; scoped in the intake CSV.
Symbol overlap: U_i also names the disturbance vertex of the causal diagram (def:p15-w02c-p15-009-causal-diagram), following the source's Fig. 1 labels; the random variable U_i keeps its meaning.

Symbol overlap (run r5): \mathcal D, \mathcal X and \mathcal G are used in Lauritzen's notation in sec:p16-measurable-causal-graphs and def:p15-w02c-p15-009-undirected-markov; check.py reports them as outside registered scopes; intake rows scope them locally. D (plain) also names the chain's six-vertex diagram in thm:p15-w02c-p15-009-chain-diagram.

Notation: the new chapter writes conditional independence with \perp, as def:p16-measurable-ci does, where Lauritzen writes a doubled perpendicular sign; the text states the difference. \perp also denotes mutual singularity of measures in other P15 chapters (different scope).

Driver insertion needed (lead): \input{parts/p15/conditioning-independence-and-information-w02c-p15-009} after the w02b-p15-008 input in handbook/parts/p15.tex and \input{annex/p15/conditioning-independence-and-information-w02c-p15-009} after the w02b-p15-008 input in handbook/annex/p15.tex.
unit_compile: ok (run b2): waves.py unit-compile reports ok, no errors, no undefined citations or unknown refs; one overfull box remains, the annex item header for the long label annex:p15-w02c-p15-009-sigma-ci-rules (17.6pt). waves.py verify: hard list empty.
existing_treatment_found_not_listed: handbook/parts/p16/causal-mediation.tex and handbook/annex/p16/causal-mediation.tex (annex:p16.mediation-four-set-criterion): the finite cross-world bridge with the same restoration sketch; not edited (not an editable host).
handbook/parts/p16/graphical-separation-adjustment.tex: def:p16-active-path, def:p16-ancestral-moral-graph, thm:p16-moral-separation-bridge, used by citation.

handbook/parts/p16/graphical-separation-adjustment.tex: thm:p16-collider-numerical-example (same two-bit common-effect table as Pearl's two coins) and the citation of Pearl's Definition 1, p. 106; linked, not duplicated.

handbook/parts/p15/finite-probability.tex def:p15-finite-independence (conditional independence given an event of positive probability) and def:p15-pairwise-not-mutual; the new chapter generalizes to sub-sigma-algebras and does not repeat them.
